To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
A robust mathematical model for the prediction of HIC retention times based on the atomic‐level hydrophilicity distribution of protein surfaces was developed.
the retention time of a protein in HIC depends on the distribution of local hydrophobicity over the surface of the protein.
a simple linear model can predict protein retention behaviour in hydrophobic‐interaction chromatography with high accuracy, based on the atomic‐level hydrophilicity distribution of the proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of the HIC behavior of proteins based on a robust statistical characterization of the atomic‐level hydrophilic‐hydrophobic surface properties of these proteins.
the development and application of a robust statistical model to characterize protein surface properties at an atomic level.
the use of statistical methods to characterize the surface properties of proteins in order to predict their retention behaviour in HIC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a robust statistical description of the protein hydrophobicity at the atomic level is an attractive and promising alternative to amino acid level descriptions.
the robust statistical characterization of atomic‐level protein surface properties has a predictive capability for the retention behaviour of globular proteins in HIC.
the retention behaviour of proteins in HIC can be predicted by the use of robust statistics describing their atomic‐level protein surface hydrophobicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we could predict the retention behaviour of proteins in HIC by a simple model that is based on the surface properties of the protein.
a robust statistical characterization of the atomic level surface properties of proteins can be used to predict their HIC behaviour.
we have developed a robust statistical model for the prediction of HIC retention times for conformationally stable proteins with known 3D structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retention behaviour of globular proteins with well‐defined 3D structures can be predicted from a robust statistical characterization of the protein surface properties on an atomic level.
we can predict protein retention times in HIC using only the atomic‐level surface structure of a protein.

the retention behaviour of globular proteins in hydrophobically modified stationary phases can be predicted with a high degree of accuracy from their atomic‐level hydrophilic and hydrophobic surface properties.
